translationRepairs: As Yan and Pu fell one after another and Suzhou and Sizhou came under repeated threat, Right Vice Director Xu Jingheng, seeing how thin the imperial guard was, urged the emperor to withdraw from the enemy's path. Qianshan dismissed the concern and led his fellow ministers to listen to the Buddhist monk Keqin preach.

As Yun and Pu fell one after another and Suzhou and Sizhou came under repeated threat, Right Vice Director Xu Jingheng, seeing how thin the imperial guard was, urged the emperor to withdraw from the enemy's path. Qianshan dismissed the concern and led his fellow ministers to listen to the Buddhist monk Keqin preach.
鄆 is Yun (Yunzhou), not "Yan"; the idiomatic text misreads the place name.

When Minister of Revenue Huang E reached the river, soldiers who heard his surname took him for Qianshan, clamored to list his crimes, and rushed forward with drawn blades. E had barely begun to protest his identity when his head was already off.

When Chief Minister of the Court of Agriculture Huang E reached the river, soldiers who heard his surname took him for Qianshan, clamored to list his crimes, and rushed forward with drawn blades. E had barely begun to protest his identity when his head was already off.
司農卿 is the Chief Minister of the Court of Agriculture, not a Minister of Revenue (戶部).
Near the end of Emperor Gaozong's reign, an edict restored the official ranks of Qianshan, Yu Shen, and Xue Ang and granted posthumous honors to their heirs.
Near the end of Emperor Gaozong's reign, an edict restored the official ranks of Qianshan, Yu Shen, and Xue Ang and granted official employment to their descendants.
錄後 means enrolling descendants for official employment, not posthumous honors to heirs.
An edict held that because Qianshan had once served as deputy marshal, his original rank alone would be restored and one son granted posthumous honors.
An edict held that because Qianshan had once served as deputy marshal, his original rank alone would be restored and one son enrolled for official employment.
錄一子 means one son was enrolled for office (protection privilege), not granted posthumous honors.
Censor Zhang Suo denounced Qianshan's treachery and, fearing harm to the new policies, was demoted to Secretariat Gentleman and soon exiled to Jiangzhou.
Censor Zhang Suo denounced Qianshan as treacherous, warning that he would harm the new administration; Zhang Suo was demoted to Secretariat Gentleman and soon exiled to Jiangzhou.
The English makes "fearing harm" the reason for Zhang Suo's demotion; the Chinese says Zhang warned Qianshan would harm the new government (恐害新政), and then Zhang (所) was demoted.
After crossing, they traveled through Daming, Yan, and Ji to Nanjing, and Boyan was recommended for appointment as Compiler in the Hall for Gathering Excellence.
After crossing, they traveled through Daming, Yun, and Ji to Nanjing, and Boyan was recommended for appointment as Compiler in the Hall for Gathering Excellence.
In the eleventh month the officials were assembled to deliberate in the Yanshe Hall; Fan Zongyin and seventy others favored cession, while Hui and thirty-six others opposed it.
In the eleventh month the officials were assembled to deliberate in the Yanhe Hall; Fan Zongyin and seventy others favored cession, while Hui and thirty-six others opposed it.
延和殿 is the Yanhe Hall; "Yanshe" is a misreading.

Earlier, after Boyan had left Xiangzhou, the Jurchens seized his son Si, Supervisor of the Directorate of Armaments, and used him to demand territory up to Xiangzhou; the defending official Zhao Bushi held firm and refused to yield, so Si was taken north and only returned after a long captivity.

Earlier, after Boyan had left Xiangzhou, the Jurchens seized his son Si, Assistant of the Directorate of Armaments, and used him to demand territory up to Xiangzhou; the defending official Zhao Bushi held firm and refused to yield, so Si was taken north and only returned after a long captivity.
軍器監丞 is the Assistant (丞) of the Directorate of Armaments, not its Supervisor.
In the second month of the first year of Shaoxing, he was appointed Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
In the second month of the first year of Shaoxing, he was appointed Assistant Councilor of State.
參知政事 is Assistant Councilor of State, not Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs (僕射).
In the second year Hui memorialized to establish a Bureau for Political Reform, appointing himself supervisor with Vice Director Zhai Ruwen as co-director.
In the second year Hui memorialized to establish a Bureau for Political Reform, appointing himself supervisor with Assistant Councilor Zhai Ruwen as co-director.
參知政事 is Assistant Councilor of State, not "Vice Director".

Hui, heedless of death by axe and halberd, argued the interests of both dynasties and urged restoring the heir to the throne to pacify the realm—not only would Great Song be blessed, but Great Jin would gain lasting benefit as well."

Hui, heedless of death by axe and halberd, argued the interests of both dynasties and urged restoring the reigning sovereign to his throne to pacify the realm—not only would Great Song be blessed, but Great Jin would gain lasting benefit as well."
嗣君 here is the reigning successor sovereign (Qinzong), not an heir apparent.

Now the Jurchens hold a great army before a city already taken and wield the power of life and death; insisting on changing the dynasty, they would have us submit. Hui would die arguing the point—not only from loyalty to his sovereign, but to make clear the interests of both states.

Now the Jurchens hold a great army before a city already taken and wield the power of life and death; they insist on changing the ruling house. Hui would die arguing the point—not only from loyalty to his sovereign, but to make clear the interests of both states.
"they would have us submit" has no basis in 必欲易姓, which only says they insist on changing the ruling surname.
Jun said, "Working with him, I have only now learned how treacherous he is."
Jun said, "Working with him, I have only now learned how benighted he is."
暗 means benighted or unperceptive, not treacherous.
Jun disagreed and therefore recommended Hui; only after sharing power did he learn how treacherous Hui was, and he never recommended him again.
Jun disagreed and therefore recommended Hui; only after sharing power did he learn how benighted Hui was, and he never recommended him again.
暗 means benighted or unperceptive, not treacherous.
Bozong was renamed Yuan, and Bojiu was renamed Yu.
Bozong was renamed Quan, and Bojiu was renamed Qu.
璩 is read Qu, not Yu; the English misreads the character.
When Ding and Hui returned as chief ministers, the emperor issued an imperial note appointing Yu as military commissioner and enfeoffing him as Duke of Wu.
When Ding and Hui returned as chief ministers, the emperor issued an imperial note appointing Qu as military commissioner and enfeoffing him as Duke of Wu.
璩 is read Qu, not Yu.
The following year Yu was finally appointed Military Commissioner of Baoda and enfeoffed as Duke of Chongguo.
The following year Qu was finally appointed Military Commissioner of Baoda and enfeoffed as Duke of Chongguo.
璩 is read Qu, not Yu.
Several days later Vice Director Liu Dazhong reported at court and spoke on the same matter.
Several days later Assistant Councilor Liu Dazhong reported at court and spoke on the same matter.
參知政事 is Assistant Councilor of State, not "Vice Director".
Hui feigned intercession on his behalf, but in the end had Quan shackled and exiled to Chaozhou.
Hui feigned intercession on his behalf, but in the end had Quan shackled and exiled to Zhaozhou.
昭州 is Zhaozhou; "Chaozhou" is 潮州, a different prefecture.
Because Vice Director Li Guang had long enjoyed public esteem, he was made to endorse the peace proclamation to suppress loose talk.
Because Assistant Councilor Li Guang had long enjoyed public esteem, he was made to endorse the peace proclamation to suppress loose talk.
參知政事 is Assistant Councilor of State, not "Vice Director".
Drafting Reviewer Lou Zhao also cited the precedent of 'three years of mourning without speaking' to inform Hui; thereupon the plan was settled for Hui to act as chief mourner and receive the letter.

Drafting Reviewer Lou Zhao also cited the precedent of 'three years of mourning without speaking' to inform Hui; thereupon the plan was settled for Hui to act as regent chief minister (zhongzai) and receive the letter.
攝塚宰 means acting as the regent chief minister during mourning, not acting as chief mourner.
When the Veritable Records of Emperor Huizong were completed, he was transferred to Junior Preceptor and additionally enfeoffed as Duke of Ji.
When the Veritable Records of Emperor Huizong were completed, he was transferred to Junior Guardian and additionally enfeoffed as Duke of Ji.
少保 is Junior Guardian; Junior Preceptor is 少師.

Credentialed Gentleman Zhang Xingcheng presented twenty chapters of Inquiry of the Humble, arguing that from antiquity peace negotiations have never remained unchanged, and listing preparatory strategies for every contingency.

Gentleman of Meritorious Achievement Zhang Xingcheng presented twenty chapters of Inquiry of the Humble, arguing that from antiquity peace negotiations have never remained unchanged, and listing preparatory strategies for every contingency.
迪功郎 is the Gentleman of Meritorious Achievement; "Credentialed Gentleman" renders a different rank (承信郎).
In the eleventh month Li Guang was demoted to Tengzhou and Fan Tong was dismissed as Vice Director.
In the eleventh month Li Guang was demoted to Tengzhou and Fan Tong was dismissed as Assistant Councilor.
參知政事 is Assistant Councilor of State, not "Vice Director".
Imperial Academy student Zhang Boli once wrote on a wall, "Fuchai, have you forgotten that the King of Yue killed your father?" He was beaten on the back, tattooed, and exiled to Jiyang Army.
Imperial Academy student Zhang Bolin once wrote on a wall, "Fuchai, have you forgotten that the King of Yue killed your father?" He was beaten on the back, tattooed, and exiled to Jiyang Army.
張伯麟 is Zhang Bolin; the final syllable of the given name was dropped.
In the sixth month Credentialed Gentleman Wang Tinggui was placed under supervised exile at Chenzhou for composing a poem to send off Hu Quan.
In the sixth month Gentleman of Meritorious Achievement Wang Tinggui was placed under supervised exile at Chenzhou for composing a poem to send off Hu Quan.
迪功郎 is the rank Gentleman of Meritorious Achievement; "Credentialed Gentleman" is a mistranslation.
In the sixth month Xi was made Junior Preceptor.
In the sixth month Xi was made Junior Guardian.
少保 is Junior Guardian; "Junior Preceptor" renders 少師.

Right Credentialed Gentleman An Cheng and commoner Wang Dagui were placed under supervised exile; the hereditary beneficiary Hui Jun and Advance Righteousness Vice Warrant Officer Liu Yunzhong were executed; the Jingshan monk Qingyan was tattooed—all for slander.

Right Gentleman of Meritorious Achievement An Cheng and commoner Wang Dagui were placed under supervised exile; the hereditary beneficiary Hui Jun and Advance Righteousness Vice Warrant Officer Liu Yunzhong were executed; the Jingshan monk Qingyan was tattooed—all for slander.
右迪功郎 is Right Gentleman of Meritorious Achievement; "Credentialed Gentleman" is a mistranslation.
In the twenty-first year Palace Attendant Wang Yangying submitted a memorial recommending Xi as chief minister; Hui memorialized to appoint Yangying Prefect of Taizhou.
In the twenty-first year Gentleman for Court Service Wang Yangying submitted a memorial recommending Xi as chief minister; Hui memorialized to appoint Yangying Prefect of Taizhou.
朝散郎 is the prestige rank Gentleman for Court Service, not "Palace Attendant".
In the eighteenth year Xi was appointed Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs; Hui asked Hu Ning, "What is the outside talk?"
In the eighteenth year Xi was appointed Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs; Hui asked Hu Ning, "What is the outside talk?"
知樞密院事 is Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs; "Commissioner" renders 樞密使.
In the twenty-second year four great cases were opened against Wang Shu's two sons Zhiqi and Zhi, Ye Sansheng, Yang Wei, and Yuan Minqiu—all punished for slander.
In the twenty-second year four great cases were opened against Wang Shu's two sons Zhiqi and Zhixun, Ye Sansheng, Yang Wei, and Yuan Minqiu—all punished for slander.
之荀 is Zhixun; the name was truncated to "Zhi".

On withdrawing he sought the reason and learned the Prince of Jin'an had spoken; he memorialized that the Prince, residing in the Xiuwang residence during mourning, should not receive salary, reducing him by two hundred strings of cash per month—the emperor provided it from the inner treasury.

On withdrawing he sought the reason and learned the Prince of Jin'an had spoken; he memorialized that the Prince, being in mourning for Prince Xiu, should not receive salary, reducing him by two hundred strings of cash per month—the emperor provided it from the inner treasury.
居秀王喪 means observing mourning for Prince Xiu, not residing in a "Xiuwang residence".
eunuch Pei Yong was punished for pointing and reproaching, and assigned to supervised exile at Qiongzhou.
eunuch Pei Yong was punished for slandering the throne, and assigned to supervised exile at Qiongzhou.
指斥 here means insulting the sovereign, not literal "pointing and reproaching".
In the second month of the twenty-fourth year Yang Ju, because his younger brother Wei had died of overwork at Binzhou on an old case, was assigned to supervised exile at Yongzhou.
In the second month of the twenty-fourth year Yang Ju, because his younger brother Wei had died at Binzhou under an earlier case, was assigned to supervised exile at Yongzhou.
舊累死 means he died under an earlier implication; "overwork" is not in the source.
On the yimwei day of that month the emperor visited Hui's residence to inquire after his illness; Hui said not a word and only wept.
On the yiwei day of that month the emperor visited Hui's residence to inquire after his illness; Hui said not a word and only wept.
乙未 is romanized yiwei; "yimwei" is a typo.

In their fabrications, when no crime could be described, they said only slander, pointing and reproach, resentment and longing, forming factions to seek fame—and in extreme cases, having a heart without a ruler.

In their fabrications, when no crime could be described, they said only slander, insulting the sovereign, resentment and longing, forming factions to seek fame—and in extreme cases, having a heart without a ruler.
指斥 means insulting the sovereign, not literal "pointing and reproach".
Affairs of commanderies and kingdoms were reported only to the provinces—not one reached the throne.
Affairs of commanderies and kingdoms were reported only to the Department of State Affairs—not one reached the throne.
省 here is the central Department (Secretariat), not "the provinces".
